newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Navajo coal-fired unit back up to 720 MW.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Navajo coal-fired unit back up to 720 MW.

text.p: The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant in Page, Ariz., was back up to 720 MW after tripping off-line early Monday, sources familiar with the plant said Tuesday.
The incident was termed a "mystery trip" and efforts to restart the unit began early Monday afternoon.
Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.
The plant is operated by Salt River Project, which also holds a 21.7-percent equity stake.
Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, Arizona Public Service Co, Nevada Power and Tucson Electric Power.
